summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would raise fee limits so the corporate regulator can recover its costs for supervising financial services.
The package would let the regulator set different fees depending on the type of entity and the complexity of the application, and charge extra for changing or cancelling an auditor's registration.
The explanatory memorandum does not specify the new fee caps or the start date.
changes: Raise the maximum fees the regulator can charge for its supervisory work.
Let the regulator set different fees based on entity type and application complexity.
Allow the regulator to charge extra fees for changing or cancelling a self-managed super fund auditor's registration.
summary.affected: Companies and other entities regulated by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, and approved SMSF auditors.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: This bill amends the Credit Fees Act to allow ASIC to charge different fees based on the type of entity, enabling full cost recovery for specific regulatory activities such as processing licence or registration applications. Complementary amendments are made in three related bills.

speeches.speaker: Jason Falinski
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Corporations (Fees) Amendment (ASIC Fees) Bill 2018, arguing it will increase fee caps, expand chargeable matters, and introduce an industry funding model to make ASIC more efficient, transparent, and accountable while shifting costs from taxpayers to fee recipients.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The government introduced the second phase of the ASIC industry funding model, effective from 1 July 2018, to recover regulatory costs directly attributable to specific entities through cost-reflective fees, replacing nominal fees previously subsidised by taxpayers.
